correctness.rationale: For any single-pass initially periodic state, summed pre-first-firing eligibility inequalities give mn>=mn+e_same; so every round contains firing vertices from only one shore, with zero mass slack. Two successive firing rounds from one shore would make a future firer already eligible previously, contradicting uniqueness. Thus cyclic alternation and ordered nonempty partitions are forced. The chip value of a vertex is its number of later-firing neighbors. Conversely the ordered-block construction has mass mn, the specified unique firing sequence and period exactly 2k. Distinctness recovers firing order from unique initial wave values; multiply 2(k! S(m,k))(k! S(n,k)), divide by period for orbit count. Direct independent simulations enumerate all mass-mn states for nine graphs and reconstruct partitions for five. These computations support but do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: Exact natural per-period recurrent-state and orbit counts at the critical chip total |E|, not merely attainable periods. The structural characterization by ordered nonempty alternating shore blocks yields an infinite two-parameter Stirling distribution, with previously uncounted period-six-and-higher waves and maximal-period orbit census. Example K3,3 has 72 distinct period-six states/12 cycles. This is a motivated critical-energy observable in the deterministic fixed-energy sandpile, rather than an arbitrary slice of parameters; existing sampled period constructions and smaller-period polynomials do not directly answer it.
